School of Electronics and Computer Science, University of Southampton; OpenAlex dates it 2026-07-02. Every odd n has a unique n = lambda*2^a*3^b - 1 with gcd(lambda,6) = 1 and a >= 1, giving a coordinate (a,b) on skeletons L_lambda, with row k = a + b preserved and the flow (a,b) -> (a-1,b+1). WHAT IT ANTICIPATES, and why this record exists: Proposition 3.11 (Growth rate) proves (n'+1)/(n+1) = 3/2 exactly along the diagonal -- that IS the statement that u = x+1 conjugates the Collatz odd step to u -> 3u/2, and its proof text explicitly links the 3/2 map to Flatto's beta-transformation literature, which is this laboratory's own position on the Mahler cluster reached independently. Corollary 3.9 gives the interior step count, a - 1 steps from (a,b) to the boundary, which is Lemma 8's run length in her coordinates. Theorem 3.6 says the interior needs no number-theoretic input and v_2(3n+1) = 1 always there, concentrating the difficulty at the boundary a = 1, where Proposition 3.10 gives v_2(3n+1) = 1 + v_2(lambda*3^(b+1) - 1). A LABEL CORRECTION, made here against the source: claude/exponent-floor-3n1-2adic-mvwa96 attributes the conjugation to 'Theorem 3.6 / Prop 3.11'; read in the paper, the conjugation is Proposition 3.11 and Theorem 3.6 is the interior/boundary statement.
